name: Hadad
overview: Hadad was a male member of the tribe named after him and is uniquely identified as the eighth-born son of Ishmael. Scripture records him specifically by his birth order among Ishmael's sons, highlighting his place in the genealogy of Ishmael's descendants. No additional notes are given about his life or deeds.
namesAndTitles: The name Hadad means 'sharp' or 'fierce,' reflecting a strong and possibly formidable character. This proper name is not indicated as being given by God but is recorded in Genesis 25:15. The meaning of his name may suggest attributes valued in his tribal context.
familyAndRelationships: Hadad is explicitly identified as a son of Ishmael, making him part of the lineage descending from Abraham through Ishmael. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not provide further family details or relationships for Hadad.
scriptureSignificance: Hadad's significance lies primarily in his genealogical role as one of Ishmael's sons, contributing to the fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham regarding numerous descendants. His place as the eighth-born son situates him within the broader narrative of God's covenantal blessings extending beyond Isaac's line. Although no specific actions or events are recorded about Hadad, his mention preserves the continuity of Ishmael's lineage in Scripture.
